title: Chapter 2 — The Night Bus
description: Lagos at 5:40 a.m. Ike's spare-parts 'business'. The first phone call from home. Chief Ọ̀dụ̀'s party, where nobody laughs.

cards.title: Lagos
cards.text: 5:40 a.m. Iyana-Wahala bus stop. The bus doors open and the city hits you in the face like a wet towel full of noise.

beats.speaker: fakeConductor
beats.text: Welcome to Lagos! Loading fee! Everybody wey enter Lagos pays ₦500 loading fee! Government law!

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: (He has a receipt book. The receipts are blank.)

options.text: Pay him. You don't want trouble on your first day.
"I came from the village, not from yesterday."

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: (an old agbero with three fingers, watching) Hm. JJC. Rule number one: in Lagos, nobody gives you a receipt for nothing. Where you dey go?

variants.text: (an old agbero with three fingers, laughing) Ehen! This JJC get sense. Rule number one, and you knew it before I taught you. Where you dey go?

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: Ike Okafor's shop. Spare parts. Ọjà market.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: Ike Money? (His face changes.) Hm. Go well, my son. And... if he takes you to a party where everybody wears white, come and find me first.

beats.objective: Find Ike's spare-parts shop in the market.

beats.speaker: ike
beats.text: You came! (He looks at your bag, then at your face.) The fee. Let me see it.

variants.text: Mr Yahoo-detector! You came. Let me see the fee before you investigate my business again.

beats.speaker: ike
beats.text: (He grabs your hand and turns it over.) Quarry hands. Lagos doesn't respect quarry hands. We'll fix that.

beats.speaker: ike
beats.text: Correct! Now you're inside. Spare parts by day. Other things by night. Don't ask which is which.

beats.speaker: ike
beats.text: Short. You brought short money to Lagos. (He takes what you have anyway, and gives back ₦2,000.) Then you start as a boy. No salary. You sleep in the shop with the rats. The rats pay rent. You don't.

cards.title: Ọjà market
cards.text: Weeks. Brake pads, fan belts, "original" Toyota parts made in a factory that has never heard of Toyota. Ike is gone most nights.

beats.speaker: ike
beats.text: Tonight I have something for you. Choose. I don't have all day, my driver is idling.

beats.speaker: ike
beats.text: "What will it be?"

options.text: Drive a package across Lagos in the shop's bus. Don't open it.
Sell the 'original' parts to the drivers. They're fake.
"I'll sweep the shop and learn the real trade."

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A taped box, heavier than it looks. Ike says it's 'documents'. Documents don't usually tick. (It doesn't tick. You just keep listening for it.)

beats.speaker: bassey
beats.text: (opening the box with a pen) Hm. Fake customs papers. Who sent you? ...Don't answer. I can see from your face you don't know. I am writing your face in my book.

beats.speaker: ike
beats.text: (an hour later, after a phone call and an envelope) You got caught. Me, I never get caught. Learn.

beats.speaker: ike
beats.text: The package is where? (He breathes very slowly.) Somebody is going to ask me that question. And I am going to give them your name.

beats.speaker: ike
beats.text: Sweep. Okay. Sweep, Mr Conscience. (But the next morning he shows you how to read a part number. And how to spot a fake. He doesn't say why.)

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Midnight. Your phone rings. NNE.

beats.speaker: nneEmeka
beats.text: {name}. You don't call. I sold my good wrapper to pay the oil women. (She doesn't say it to hurt you. That's why it hurts.)

beats.speaker: nneEmeka
beats.text: {name}. I found the ₦5,000 under my pillow. You think I didn't know? Foolish boy. My foolish boy.

beats.speaker: nneEmeka
beats.text: You told me you would find work here, at home. And then you left. I'm not angry. I'm just... the house is quiet.

beats.speaker: nneEmeka
beats.text: Somebody has fenced Papa's land. Dozie says... Dozie says you sold it. Tell me it's a lie. Tell me and I will believe you.

beats.speaker: nneEmeka
beats.text: (She will believe you. That's the worst part.)

options.text: "It's a lie, Nne. Dozie is lying."
"I sold it. I'm sorry. I'll buy it back."

beats.speaker: nneEmeka
beats.text: (a long silence) Okay. Okay. Eat well, my son.

beats.speaker: nneEmeka
beats.text: And Ọnyịsị came. He asks when Mega Fortune will pay the harvest money back. He is smiling, but his smile is tired.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: (The school roof is still leaking.)

options.text: "There is no Mega Fortune. Tell him I will pay it back myself."

beats.speaker: nneEmeka
beats.text: They are saying you tried to steal the harvest money. In front of the elders. My son... I don't go to the market any more.

beats.speaker: nneEmeka
beats.text: They say you ran. Through the stream. With the whole village behind you. Even the goats are talking.

beats.speaker: nneEmeka
beats.text: Ọnyịsị says you owe the village ₦20,000, and that he respects you. Strange man. Strange thing.

beats.speaker: chinwe
beats.text: (a message, then a call) Have you found a room? You said a year. I'm counting. I'm good at counting.

beats.speaker: chinwe
beats.text: You said double. I'm not asking for double. I'm asking how you are.

beats.speaker: chinwe
beats.text: You didn't take my money. I keep thinking about that. Most men would have.

beats.speaker: chinwe
beats.text: You told me not to wait. So I'm not waiting. I'm just... calling. That's different.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Ike's voice from the shop door: "Wear your best shirt tomorrow. We're going to a party. Chief Ọ̀dụ̀'s party."

cards.title: Zone 5
cards.text: A gate that opens by itself. A garden with lights in the trees. Men and women in white, drinking from gold-rimmed glasses. Everybody is smiling.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Nobody is laughing. You notice it the way you notice a clock that has stopped.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The music is loud. The smiles are louder. It takes you a while to realise what's missing: laughter.

beats.speaker: chiefOdu
beats.text: Ike's boy. (He looks at you the way a tailor looks at cloth.) Hungry eyes. I like hungry eyes. They see further.

beats.speaker: chiefOdu
beats.text: "What do you want in Lagos, young man?"

beats.speaker: chiefOdu
beats.text: (He smiles without moving any other part of his face.) We will see each other again. Everybody does.

variants.text: (For a moment the whole garden goes quiet.) Laughing is for people who can afford to waste breath. We will see each other again, young man.

beats.title: End of Chapter 2 — The Night Bus
beats.summary: Lagos has your name now. Money {money}. Conscience {stat:conscience}. Ike's trust {stat:ikeTrust}. Chief Ọ̀dụ̀ has noticed you.
